title: Understanding Your EL2 Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion Guide
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary for an EL2 salary or any role. Use our calculator with a 38-hour week, tax, super, and fortnightly pay estimates.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, your annual salary is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours (38 × 52).

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary for an EL2 position?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, if your hourly rate is $50, your annual salary would be $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. The Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool can help confirm the correct award rate for your classification.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates for EL2 roles?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is the base rate for award/agreement-free employees. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Award rates, such as those in the Professional Employees Award or the APS Enterprise Agreement, often set higher minimums for skilled roles like EL2. EL2 salaries in the Australian Public Service are typically well above the National Minimum Wage and often exceed the ABS average weekly ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 (May 2026). Always check your specific award or agreement for your correct rate.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my EL2 salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation Guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual salary is $100,000, your employer would contribute an additional $12,000 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your salary; it is paid in addition. The Australian Taxation Office sets the rules and caps.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to an Annual Salary

Whether you're negotiating an EL2 salary in the Australian Public Service or comparing a contract role, understanding how your hourly rate translates to an annual figure is essential. Our calculator uses the standard formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For full-time employees, we assume a 38-hour week, as defined by the Fair Work Commission for the National Minimum Wage. This gives you a gross annual salary before tax, super, and other deductions.

### The Formula in Practice

Let's say your hourly rate is $60. For a 38-hour week, your weekly pay is $60 × 38 = $2,280. Multiply by 52 weeks to get an annual salary of $118,560. If you work a different number of hours per week, adjust accordingly. For example, a 40-hour week would give $60 × 40 × 52 = $124,800. Our calculator lets you enter your actual hours per week for a custom result.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. Using the example above, $2,280 per week becomes $4,560 per fortnight. This can help you budget and compare with job advertisements that quote fortnightly figures.

## National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates vs. EL2 Salaries

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal minimum for award/agreement-free employees. However, most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher rates. For example, the *Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award* has specific pay rates for different classifications.

An EL2 salary is a common benchmark for senior APS roles. While there is no single published EL2 rate in the sources we use, EL2 salaries are typically well above the National Minimum Wage and often exceed the ABS average weekly ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 (May 2026). Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool can help you see how any hourly rate compares to these benchmarks.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, this means a casual rate of $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). Our calculator includes a checkbox to add casual loading automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – use the base rate and let the tool add the loading.

## Tax and Medicare

Your gross annual salary is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies a progressive tax scale for 2026–27:
- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimator applies these rates to give you an approximate net annual and fortnightly amount. Note that the Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles are based on 2025–26 figures, as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of calculation.

## Superannuation

Superannuation Guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on a $100,000 salary, your employer contributes an extra $12,000 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrifice can affect your take-home pay.

## Important Disclaimer

The annual pay shown by our calculator is an estimate based on the formula: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For precise rates, always refer to your award or enterprise agreement. The Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool can provide personalised information based on your classification and circumstances.

## Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) is the home page where you enter your base hourly rate. Check the box for casual loading if applicable. The tool then calculates your annual salary, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. It's designed for quick comparisons – whether you're evaluating an EL2 salary offer or checking your current rate against the National Minimum Wage.

### Summary

- **Annual gross** = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours if full-time)
- **Fortnightly gross** = weekly pay × 2
- **National Minimum Wage** (1 July 2026): $26.44/hr, $1,004.90/week
- **Casual loading**: 25% on top of base rate
- **Super**: 12% paid on top, up to $270,830
- **Tax**: Progressive scale with $18,200 tax-free threshold

Use our [reference tables](/data) to see how your rate compares to industry benchmarks, or check the [pay guides](/blog) for your award.
